editorial_disclaimer: Independent historical interpretation. No NASA endorsement or affiliation is implied.

records.label: BEFORE / THE TEST
records.title: An unfueled rocket was not a safe cabin.
records.summary: Apollo 1's plugs-out rehearsal was a ground test. The absence of Saturn IB fuel did not remove risks inside Command Module 012.
records.finding: The crew occupied a spacecraft whose ground-test conditions and emergency egress procedures were later judged hazardous. The crew photograph establishes personnel and period—not cabin fire-safety conditions.
records.limit: A training photograph cannot prove cabin atmosphere, test approval decisions or the point of ignition; those findings come from the Apollo 204 Review Board.
records.image_description: Apollo 1 crew Gus Grissom, Ed White II and Roger Chaffee standing outside near Launch Complex 34 during training.

records.label: BEFORE / THE ATMOSPHERE
records.title: The atmosphere amplified the danger.
records.summary: The Review Board documented a 100% oxygen cabin atmosphere at 16.7 psia. Oxygen intensified combustion; it was not itself an ignition spark.
records.finding: The 1967 Board called the test conditions extremely hazardous. Its findings—not the accompanying January 3 spacecraft-preparation photograph—establish the cabin's atmosphere.
records.limit: The preparation photograph cannot depict oxygen concentration or pressure. Do not treat it as a sensor trace.
records.image_description: Command/Service Module 012 being moved for mating to the Saturn Lunar Module Adapter at Kennedy Space Center.

records.label: RECORDED / THE REPORT
records.title: The first report fixed a point in time.
records.summary: The crew's first transmission reporting fire began at approximately 23:31:04.7 GMT. It does not establish the exact instant of ignition.
records.finding: The Board correlated voice tapes and instrument telemetry. The NASA S66-58038 photograph shows an earlier altitude-chamber rehearsal, not the final test or a recording of the fire.
records.limit: Do not recast a 1966 crew-training image as 1967 fire telemetry. A reported event is not necessarily its initiating event.
records.image_description: The Apollo 1 crew preparing to enter Command Module 012 in an altitude chamber during training.

records.label: RECORDED / THE PRESSURE
records.title: Pressure outran the escape procedure.
records.summary: The Board places pressure-vessel rupture around 23:31:19 GMT, after pressure rose beyond sensor range; the hatch could not be opened before rupture.
records.finding: Board estimates indicate rupture at at least 29 psia. NASA's 2017 tribute photograph depicts a museum-era spacecraft mockup/hatch display, not footage of the 1967 rupture.
records.limit: The photograph provides later exhibition context. The rupture timing and pressure are investigative findings, not values inferred from an image.
records.image_description: Apollo 1 tribute spacecraft mockup and hatch display photographed at Kennedy Space Center in 2017.

records.label: INVESTIGATION / THE GAP
records.title: No single ignition source was proved.
records.summary: The Board judged an electrical arc the most probable initiator, but concluded that no single ignition source was conclusively identified.
records.finding: Post-fire examination documented damaged hardware and potential arcing. The NASA S67-21294 photograph records fire damage to the command-module interior the following day.
records.limit: Visible heat damage is not a photograph of the initiating arc. The exact wire, location and instant of ignition remain unproven.
records.image_description: Interior of Command Module 012 after the Apollo 1 fire, showing intense heat damage.

records.label: AFTER / THE RESPONSE
records.title: One hatch became part of a larger redesign.
records.summary: The program adopted a faster outward-opening hatch and a broad set of material, wiring, testing and rescue changes.
records.finding: NASA's 2017 tribute image shows the redesigned hatch displayed in the museum. The Review Board records the underlying safety recommendations and broader failure of risk classification.
records.limit: The 2017 display is not an image of the 1967 accident itself. The changes cannot be reduced to the hatch alone.
records.image_description: Redesigned outward-opening Apollo hatch exhibited at the Apollo 1 tribute at Kennedy Space Center.
